key_insight: MedGame turns static medical cases into interactive storytelling games powered by large language models, helping learners make decisions across an entire clinical trajectory rather than answering isolated questions. It reframes medical education as an executable narrative experience with structured guidance and feedback.
problem_solved: Most LLM-based medical education tools focus on single-turn Q&A or local feedback, which fails to support end-to-end clinical reasoning and decision-making. This paper addresses the need for a case-level, decision-centered learning flow that is both interactive and pedagogically structured.
method: Uses a dual-engine architecture to generate and run story-based medical learning experiences.
A Medical Narrative Designer converts clinical cases into structured narrative scenarios grounded in case facts.
An interactive game engine manages learner decisions, branches the story, and supports feedback across the full case journey.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, MedGame shows how LLMs can move beyond chatbots into curriculum-aware, interactive educational systems. It offers a reusable pattern for building structured, domain-grounded learning environments that support reasoning, engagement, and scalable practice.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing static case -> narrative design -> interactive game -> learner feedback

Icon set for patient, clinician, diagnosis, and treatment decisions
Before/after comparison of traditional Q&A tutoring vs. story-driven clinical learning
paper_title: MedGame: Storytelling Gamification Empowered by Large Language Models for Medical Education
paper_authors: Qian Wu, Xinrong Zhou, Zizhan Ma, Kai Chen, Zheyao Gao
